To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DC-SIGN and its closely related family member DC-SIGNR are down regulated during KSHV infection and this is mediated by the MARCH-family KSHV ubiquitin ligases, K3 and KSHV K5.
the C-type lectins DC-SIGN and DCSIGNR are down regulated during infection by Kaposi's Sarcoma Associated Herpesvirus (KHSV) through the viral MARCH family proteins K3 and K-5.
KSHV K3 and KSHV K5 down regulate DC-SIGN and DCSIGNR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of DC-SIGNALS by KSHV.
the molecular mechanisms of the KSHV K3 and K3 proteins and how they modulate cellular proteins to facilitate KSHV replication.
the molecular mechanisms of KSHV pathogenesis, and the role of the K3 and KSHV K5 proteins in the regulation of host immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the KSHVs K3 and KSHV K5 proteins are both able to target DC-SIGN and the closely related DC- SIGNR, but with differing efficiency, and that these two proteins are likely important for down regulation of these lectins during KSHV infection, which may be important for the virus to establish a successful infection.

the K3 and K6 proteins of KSHV target DC-SIGN and the closely related DC- SIGNR, and that these viral proteins are important in the regulation of DC-Sign and DC-SIGN expression during viral infection.
K3 and K6 are able to down modulate both DC-SIGNR and DC-SIGN in both HEK-293 and THP-1 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K3 and K6 are able to target DC-SIGN and/or DC-SIGNR for down regulation and subsequent degradation, which is important for the virus to establish and maintain a productive infection.
DC-SIGN and its closely related receptor DC-SIGNR are targeted for down modulation following infection with KSHV by the viral MARCH-family proteins K3 and K3.
KSHV encodes two proteins, K3 and K4, that target DC-SIGN and K5 that targets DC-SIGNR, and that these proteins are important for viral infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KSHVs have evolved multiple mechanisms for down regulation of the C-type lectins, including DC-SIGN and its related receptor DC-SIGNR.
